name: AISHELL-4
notes: Paper Table 1: average overlap ratio 19.04% (train) and 9.31% (evaluation). OpenSLR names the evaluation set test

name: AISHELL-5
status_note: Lab copy of the training set (train.tar.gz) on the lab's shared corpus storage; Dev and Eval not there
notes: More than 100 hours (OpenSLR: more than 100 hours; Train 94 h, Dev 3.3 h, Eval1 and Eval2). The lab copy holds train.tar.gz only.

name: AliMeeting
status_note: Lab copy of all splits: Train_Ali (far and near), Eval_Ali and Test_Ali (far and near), TextGrid annotations. No RTTM yet
notes: Paper Table 1: average overlap ratio 42.27% (Train) and 34.20% (Eval; the text says 34.76%). Test set has far-field audio only

name: AMI Meeting Corpus
status_note: Lab copy: 173 meeting directories (Array1 audio for 169, headsets) plus the NXT annotations (687 segments files). No RTTM: speaker segments must be converted from annotations/segments
notes: Official partitions (datasets.shtml): Scenario-only (98/20/20 meetings; assume it when a paper does not say), Full-corpus (adds non-scenario meetings) and Full-corpus-ASR (about 81 h train, 9 h dev+eval). By the split rule, the train part trains and dev and eval evaluate, once a partition is chosen

name: AphasiaBank
status_note: Lab copy on the lab's shared corpus storage. The Ground Rules say password-protected data cannot be posted on other servers or installed elsewhere: whether this shared copy is allowed needs checking with whoever holds the membership
notes: Clinical discourse of people with aphasia and controls (protocol interviews, group therapy and others). The lab copy holds English, French and Mandarin; English has Aphasia, Control, Famous, Group, NonProtocol, Script and transcripts directories. CHAT transcripts are time-linked (a sample file has 414 media bullets).

name: ASCEND: A Spontaneous Chinese-English Dataset for Code-switching in Multi-turn Conversation
status_note: Open on Hugging Face CAiRE/ASCEND (about 1.2 GB parquet).
notes: Paper: 13 speaker pairs, 49 sessions, "98 raw audio files" (two per session, one per speaker mic); only utterance clips are released, not the raw session recordings, so reconstructed timelines have silence between utterances and cross-talk is lost. Start-time reading of the file name is inferred from the example (189.900 / 5.490 matching duration 5.49), not documented. Splits are utterance-level with gender balance; whether sessions are split across sets not checked. Hong Kong collection, Mandarin-English code-switching.

name: Australian Parliamentary Speech Corpus - Proof of Concept (turns, 2026-03-30)
status_note: Open on Hugging Face stcoats/au-parliament-poc-turns-2026-03-30 (about 1.1 GB parquet).
notes: 531 turns, one sitting; speakers from Hansard XML (via OpenAustralia) matched to faster-whisper/WhisperX output by "global lexical alignment, fuzzy turn matching, and parliamentary procedural rules. A local LLM-assisted review was used for difficult speaker assignments". Not diarization-model pseudo-labels, but not manual either. Audio is embedded per turn (16 kHz mono), so a full-sitting timeline must be rebuilt from start/end; gaps and interjections between turns are absent. Parliamentary speech is mostly one speaker at a time.

name: AVA-AVD
status_note: Downloadable: videos from the CVDF S3 bucket (117 files listed in dataset/split/video.list), annotations from Google Drive. Not on the lab's shared corpus storage

name: IARPA Babel language packs
status_note: Lab copy of 25 Babel language packs on the lab's shared corpus storage. RTTM must be derived from the per-side transcripts
notes: One row for the language packs (the Cantonese pack, LDC2016S02, is about 215 hours of conversational and scripted telephone speech). The lab copy holds 25 packs, BABEL_101 to BABEL_404; scripted (read) parts are not conversational and are left out.

name: Cabin interpreted interviews (CC BY YouTube, pilot)
status_note: Open on Hugging Face doanhlt/cabin-interpreted-interviews.
notes: Segments: de-ru 0.07 h, en-ar 0.27 h, vi-en 0.06 h (test), vi-ko 0.06 h; only kept segments are released, not whole videos. Uploaded 2026-10-28. Card notes YouTube ToS restricts automated download even for CC videos.

name: CALLHOME American English Speech
status_note: Lab copy of the speech release LDC97S42 (train 80, devtest 20, evltest 20 calls, SPHERE). The transcripts (LDC97T14) were not found on the lab storage, so there is no source for speaker segments yet
notes: Catalogue: 8 kHz 2-channel u-law SPHERE (SHORTEN-compressed), calls up to 30 minutes, mostly between family members or close friends; the release holds training, development and a subset of evaluation data. Transcripts are LDC97T14. A Second Edition exists (LDC2026S08). The 1997, 1998 and 2000 HUB5 English evaluations draw on it (LDC2002S23, LDC2002S10, LDC2002S09); the 2000 HUB5 set (LDC2002S09) is on the lab storage

name: CALLHOME Spanish Speech
status_note: Lab copy of LDC96S35 (120 SPHERE files: train 80, devtest 20, evltest 20) and the transcripts LDC96T17. No RTTM: derive turns from the transcripts
notes: The catalogue gives approximately 38 hours and calls up to 30 minutes. Transcripts are a separate LDC corpus (LDC96T17)

name: 2000 NIST Speaker Recognition Evaluation (CALLHOME diarization set)
status_note: Lab copy of LDC2001S97. Not registered or measured yet; the speaker segment files in the copy have not been examined
notes: This row is the CALLHOME part of the speaker segmentation test of the 2000 NIST SRE, released as LDC2001S97. Evaluation plan (catalogue documentation): summed two-channel CALLHOME conversations in a variety of languages, up to 10 minutes and up to 10 speakers each, no more than 500 segments, on discs sid00sg1 and sid00sg2; speakers differ from those of the detection and tracking segments. The whole release (catalogue): 10,328 single-channel SPHERE files, 148.9 hours, mostly Switchboard-2; 1,426 missing files were added on 2017-06-27. The plan forbade training on the CALLHOME corpora for this evaluation, apart from the CALLHOME development CD

name: CantoMap (Cantonese MapTask corpus)
status_note: Audio + ELAN on request to the authors (G. Winterstein, UQAM); GitHub holds only maps and README.
notes: 768 min over 20 pairs (Table 4, durations 13-110 min). Recorders were per participant but participants sat ~1.5 m apart, so tracks are personal but not head-set close-talk. Jyutping tier automatic (dictionary lookup). Also a read wordlist task ("ReadingData" per README; not in the GitHub tree, which holds only maps). Code-mixing with English occurs. Participants consented to release.

name: CHiME-5
status_note: Lab copy (made in 2021): audio and transcription JSON for train, dev and eval, with the CHiME-5 non-commercial licence 1.00 PDF. No RTTM. CHiME-6 (same recordings, alignment fixed) is also on the lab storage and is recommended by the CHiME-5 page for new work
notes: Superseded: the CHiME-5 page says CHiME-6 fixes audio alignment issues of the original data and recommends CHiME-6 for any new work. Recorded with 6 Kinect arrays (4 microphones each) and 4 binaural pairs worn by the participants, in 20 homes; each party lasted at least 2 hours in kitchen, dining and living phases (paper 2.1-2.2). hours_reported and n_speakers_reported are sums of the splits in paper Table 1

name: CHiME-6
status_note: Lab copy: train 16, dev 2, eval 2 sessions with transcription JSON and LICENSE.txt (CC BY-SA 4.0). No RTTM: speaker segments must be converted from the JSON
notes: Derived from CHiME-5 by the chime6-synchronisation script (OpenSLR 150). Used in the CHiME-6 Challenge (2020) and the CHiME-7 DASR task (2023). Sizes on OpenSLR: train 97G, dev 11G, eval 12G

name: A corpus of conversational Luganda
status_note: Transcripts free on Zenodo 8432340; audio location unknown (ask the authors).
notes: Recorded in Kampala in 2019 and 2023. EAF header references "RELATIVE_MEDIA_URL=../Luganda_audio/ga_MAK_190714_FS03.wav" (the audio exists on the authors' side). A Zenodo search for the authors (Namyalo, Zellers, Witzlack-Makarevich, Lorenzen) found no audio record. Annotation method not stated. If the audio project is found, this becomes a candidate (A).

name: DataHive Conversations samples
status_note: Hugging Face, open: datahiveai/multilingual-conversations-sample plus datahiveai/{english,hindi,russian,vietnamese,indonesian,arabic,italian}-conversations-sample.
notes: Free part is small vendor samples. Multilingual repo: 61 conversations, 19h 31m 47s, 80 speakers, ~1.13 GB (API file sizes), stereo MP3 48 kHz 128 kbps. Per-language repos (all CC BY 4.0, not gated): english 10 conv / 4h 59m 50s / 20 spk; arabic 11 conv / 3h 40m 3s / 11 spk (card's count); italian 6 conv / 3h 3m 4s / 6 spk; hindi, russian, vietnamese, indonesian repos also exist (0.17-0.29 GB each, cards not read in full). The per-language en/hi/ru/vi/id repos likely overlap the multilingual repo (not checked). Metadata includes automatic overlap/turns-per-minute measures ("Labels and measurements are automatic"). Lossy (Opus then MP3). Larger custom collections are sold (contact@datahive.ai).

name: DementiaBank
status_note: Lab copy on the lab's shared corpus storage. The Ground Rules say password-protected data cannot be posted on other servers or installed elsewhere: whether this shared copy is allowed needs checking with whoever holds the membership
notes: Discourse of people with dementia and controls. The lab copy holds English (Pitt, ADReSS2020). Whether its CHAT files are time-linked was not checked.

name: Third DIHARD Speech Diarization Challenge data
notes: Two LDC releases, development LDC2022S12 and evaluation LDC2022S14, of 5-10 minute samples from 11 domains (paper 4.1). The challenge had no training set and no constraints on training data (paper 1). Evaluation set sources (LDC2022S14): ADOS clinical interviews, restaurant conversations, DCIEM/HCRC map task (LDC96S38), Digital Archive of Southern Speech (LDC2012S03), LibriVox audiobooks, 2001 ROAR meeting speech, 2001 U.S. Supreme Court arguments, Mixer 6 Speech (LDC2013S03), VAST video, YouthPoint radio. Development set sources (LDC2022S12) include Fisher CTS, LibriVox, RT-04S meeting speech (LDC2007S11, LDC2007S12) and Supreme Court arguments. The CTS recordings are unreleased Fisher English Phase II calls (paper 4.1). Overlap to check: Mixer 6, LibriVox (the source of LibriSpeech) and Fisher

name: Dinner Party Corpus (DiPCo)
status_note: Lab copy: audio and transcription JSON for dev and eval, LICENSE.txt (CDLA-Permissive 1.0, same as the paper). No RTTM. The download given in the paper (s3.amazonaws.com/dipco/DiPCo.tgz) answered 403 AccessDenied on 2026-10-31
notes: Recorded by Amazon with groups of four employee volunteers in one room; 39 time-synchronised microphones per session (4 headsets + 5 devices x 7 channels), 16 kHz WAV downsampled from 45 kHz (paper 2.2). 32 adult speakers aged 22-62, 19 male, 13 female. Sessions last 15-47 minutes and include music playback from a given time mark (Table 3). Sessions S09/S10 and S06/S07 have the same participants. The close-talk recording of P13 in S04 is noisier (2.3). Transcribers ignored other speakers on each close-talk channel, so overlapping speech is labelled per speaker. Designed after CHiME-5 (2.3)

name: DISPLACE 2023
status_note: Only the Dev set is published (Zenodo, CC BY 4.0, 1.58 GB). No release of the Eval set was found. Not on the lab's shared corpus storage
notes: Recorded at two Indian academic institutes in rooms without soundproofing, with a lapel microphone per speaker and one far-field omnidirectional desktop microphone; conversations of 30-60 minutes; 16 kHz (paper 3.1-3.2). RTTM covers both speaker and language diarization. Participants are 33% female, mostly aged 17-40. Evaluation was run in two phases (Phase-1: 20 recordings, 11.5 h; Phase-2: the full Eval set)

name: DISPLACE-M 2026
status_note: Challenge registration + signed T&C emailed to displace2026@gmail.com, then credentials. Files hosted on HF Displace-M/Displace2026.
notes: Website: "~30 hours" of interactions; Hindi-English code-mixed (HF card adds Kannada; dev set 3 is Kannada). Track 1 SD scored by DER, RTTM submissions on Codalab. HF repo Displace-M/Displace2026 (mirror praptirn/Displace2026 with identical card and file list) is NOT gated per API (gated: false) and lists Track 1 SD dev (~2.79 GB) and eval (~3.29 GB) zips; whether the zips are password-protected was not checked (not downloaded). Reference annotation format for dev not stated. Organised by LEAP Lab IISc, NITK Surathkal, UPES; Interspeech 2026.

name: Earnings-21
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage (earnings22 is, as segmented audio; it is a different dataset). Downloadable from GitHub with Git LFS
notes: RTTM for all 44 recordings was added to the repository on 2023-12-05 (rttms/, for DER evaluation); for 4341191 and 4363614 a human re-transcribed the speaker labels, so their RTTM differs from the transcripts. Recordings last 17 min to 1 h 34 min at 11.025-44.1 kHz (paper Table 1). 9 sectors from Seeking Alpha; speaker names in speaker-metadata.csv where transcriptionists gave them. Intended as an ASR evaluation benchmark; the paper has no train/test split

name: Earnings-22
status_note: Lab copy (data, kaldi, metadata.csv) on the lab's shared corpus storage
notes: Earnings calls (the survey reports about 119 h over 125 files, with token-level speaker and timestamps in the NLP files; not checked here: turn_source left empty).

name: Earnings25
status_note: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18762167 (open) and HF mirror florencejiang/earnings25 (open).
notes: `full` config "~498" h (514 calls, ~58 min each, original sample rate MP3); `segmented` 45.9 h (290 segments, no speaker turns). Card: "treat any training on this data as contamination of the benchmark". Speakers named, not role-labelled on HF; Zenodo says roles (operator, executive, analyst) are included. Turns phrase-level, no word timestamps in the release. Bloomberg; Interspeech 2026. HF mirror florencejiang/earnings25 (12.2 GB, not gated); Zenodo single zip 12.0 GB. Would be eval tier if audio rights were clear.

name: EEG hyperscanning data of 13 groups of three people engaging in different types of conversations
status_note: Open download from Zenodo 21643064 (13 zips, about 43 GB).
notes: Audio 44.1 kHz in HDF5 alongside 32-ch EEG per subject (100 Hz). Experiments 8-20 only ("Experiments 1-7 are not included"). Language not stated. VAD on the directional channels might give rough turns, but cross-talk at 2 m makes this unreliable; usable as unlabeled far-field 3-speaker audio at most.

name: Ego4D
status_note: Lab copy of Ego4D v1 (made in 2022): annotations including the AV diarization av_train.json and av_val.json, clips, full-scale video and audio. Who signed the agreement for this copy is not known; only an institutional signature lets the lab share an internal copy (maintainer and PI decision). Only the AV diarization (AVD) benchmark has speaker segments
notes: Ego4D: 3,670 hours of daily-life egocentric video from 931 camera wearers in 74 locations and 9 countries; only portions have audio (paper abstract). Diarization labels exist only for the Audio-Visual Diarization (AVD) benchmark (github.com/EGO4D/audio-visual): about 50 h annotated out of >750 h of conversational data, 572 clips of 5 minutes, on average 4.71 speakers per clip and 0.74 per frame, the camera wearer speaking 77.64 s per clip (README). Annotations: face boxes, active speaker labels, voice_segments per person, English transcripts. 2022 challenges on eval.ai: audio-video and audio-only diarization

name: EgoCom (Egocentric Communications)
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Download script in the GitHub repository
notes: 38.5 hours (README) of natural multi-person conversations recorded from each participant's wearable (audio and video). Speaker labels are per second and described as noisy; human transcriptions exist. Whether the dataset files carry terms beyond the repository's MIT licence was not checked (the survey reported a modified MIT licence).

name: Expresso
status_note: Lab copy (audio_48khz, splits, VAD_segments.txt) on the lab's shared corpus storage
notes: Expressive speech: read utterances and improvised dialogues. Only the improvised dialogues are conversational; the survey reports a channel per speaker for them, not checked here: turn_source left empty.

name: A dataset of simulated patient-physician medical interviews with a focus on respiratory cases (Fareez et al.)
status_note: Free download from figshare (Data.zip, about 1 GB).
notes: 214 respiratory, 46 musculoskeletal, 5 cardiac, 6 gastrointestinal, 1 dermatology case. Role-played OSCE (simulated patients), real recorded speech. Forced alignment of the speaker-prefixed transcripts could produce turns (would be forced_alignment, not provided). Survey lead: an HF repack (gated, manual) adds Deepgram diarized JSON (pseudo-labels) under cc-by-4.0; I did not locate/reopen that repo. Hours not stated in the paper.

name: Fearless Steps Challenge corpus (Apollo, FS-1 to FS-4)
status_note: Challenge data via the FSC registration (NIST OpenSAT portal for P3/P4) or by form/email to FearlessSteps@utdallas.edu; the 19k-hour raw corpus is public under NASA Media Usage Guidelines.
notes: Apollo-11 challenge corpus built from 5 of 29 channels (FD, MOCR, GNC, NTWK, EECOM) over Lift Off (25 h), Lunar Landing (50 h), Lunar Walking (25 h); "Total speech content in the challenge corpus amounts to approximately 36 hours"; audio "sampled from 8Khz". FSC-4 page: "110-hour Challenge Corpus from Apollo 11" plus "10 hours of previously unreleased Apollo-8" and "5 hours of Apollo-13"; FSC-4 hosted with NIST (web portal) and LDC (data). Each channel is a loop with a primary owner plus backroom staff, so a stream is multi-speaker radio/intercom audio (domain and recording setup left blank: no enum fits). Annotation file format not read on these pages.

name: Fisher English Training Speech Part 1
status_note: Lab copy of LDC2004S13 (5850 SPHERE files) with the transcripts LDC2004T19 (fe_03_p1_tran). Part 2 is fisher_english_part2. RTTM must be derived from the per-channel transcripts
notes: Fisher protocol: platform-initiated calls of up to 10 minutes between paired strangers on a daily-assigned topic (catalogue). Parts 1 and 2 together: 11,699 conversations, about 1,960 hours; 6,813 female and 5,104 male participants over the whole collection. Turn boundaries are automatic (LDC transcripts, about 12%) or forced-aligned (BBN/WordWave), so derived RTTM inherits their errors; the LDC segmenter may have missed utterances (fe_03_readme.txt). The transcripts' call table was corrected on 2017-06-14 (fe_03_p1_calldata.tbl). fisher_meetings_sim is built from Fisher utterances

name: Fisher English Training Part 2, Speech
status_note: Lab copy of LDC2005S13 (5849 SPHERE files, fe_03_p2_sph1-7) with the transcripts LDC2005T19 (fe_03_p2_tran; conversations fe_03_05851 to fe_03_11699). RTTM must be derived from the per-channel transcripts
notes: Second half of the 2003 Fisher English collection; Part 1 is fisher_english_part1 (fe_03_00001 to fe_03_05850). Together 11,699 conversations, about 1,960 hours. Turn boundaries are automatic (LDC, about 12%) or forced-aligned (BBN/WordWave), never placed by hand. fisher_meetings_sim draws on this part too. Not checked: whether DIHARD III's CTS domain (unreleased Fisher Phase II calls, per its paper) overlaps with these calls

name: synth-fisher-meetings
status_note: Lab-internal simulation on scratch storage, which is purged: copy the clean and reverb conditions to permanent storage before relying on it. Lhotse manifests (recordings, supervisions, cuts) per condition; no RTTM yet. Lives outside SD_DATA_ROOT
notes: Four conditions of 3000 meetings each: clean, noise, reverb, noise_reverb (the same meetings under each). Speech-hours union 23.94% overlapped; 3976486 supervisions with word alignments. Sources counted from the clean supervisions: 8400 speakers, from 10209 Fisher calls, fe_03_00001 to fe_03_11699 (Parts 1 and 2). Manifests store absolute audio paths

name: Fisher Spanish Speech
status_note: Lab copy of LDC2010S01 and LDC2010T04 on the lab's shared corpus storage. RTTM must be derived from the transcripts (time stamps per channel)
notes: Speech LDC2010S01, transcripts LDC2010T04 (roughly 163 hours, approximate). The lab copy holds both, together with CALLHOME Spanish (LDC96S35, LDC96T17), in one directory.

name: GaMMA Corpus (Gaze, Motion, and Multi-talker Audio)
status_note: Open download from Zenodo record 18343509 (about 64 GB in total; close-mic + VAD about 29 GB).
notes: Conditions: 55; 65; Quiet; iLombard/Varying (quiet and cocktail-party noise). Closemic raw 48 kHz, processed 16 kHz; Group 09 lacks calibration. Hours not stated. Full annotations said to be at Dryad doi 10.5061/dryad.r7sqv9snc ("in review, DOI not active yet") and described in SIGDIAL 2025 paper. Aalborg University + GN Store Nord.

name: Gridspace-Stanford Harper Valley speech dataset
status_note: Lab copy of the SLUE-HVB subset (dev, fine-tune, test) on the lab's shared corpus storage; the full release is on GitHub
notes: Customer-service calls between agents and callers. The lab copy is SLUE-HVB, a subset with one wav per utterance plus TSV files giving each utterance's call, channel, start and duration, so call timelines can be rebuilt; the full original release on GitHub has whole calls.

name: HCRC Map Task Corpus
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Downloadable from the Edinburgh Map Task page
notes: Task-oriented two-person dialogues (one participant describes a route on a map). Whether the NXT timings are utterance-level was not checked; the per-speaker mono channels allow VAD in any case.

name: 2000 HUB5 English Evaluation Speech and Transcripts
status_note: Lab copy of LDC2002S09 and LDC2002T43 on the lab's shared corpus storage. RTTM must be derived from the transcripts
notes: About 11 hours (catalogue: approximately 11 hours) of conversational telephone speech from the 2000 HUB5 evaluation. The CALLHOME American English catalogue says the 2000 HUB5 set draws on it; overlap with callhome_american_english has not been checked.

name: Indic High-Fidelity MultiSpeaker ASR (Humyn Labs)
status_note: Hugging Face, open.
notes: Hours not stated: "Typical Duration: 10–30 minutes per recording", 37 recordings, ~1.07 GB parquet. WAV 16 kHz mono. YAML language list (hi, ml, mr, te, ta, bn, kn, bh, as, gu, pa) differs from the body list of 14; body list used. Likely a vendor sample (contact support@humynlabs.ai).

name: Indian Broadcast News Debate (IBND) Corpus
status_note: Open download from Zenodo 8161172 (single 25 GB zip).
notes: "The typical duration of each debate varies from 20 to 60 minutes." Authors Baghel, Prasanna, Guha (IIT Guwahati / Dharwad). Overlap annotation exists, which is useful for overlap detection, but no evidence of speaker-ID turns. Marked no_speaker_segments on the record text only; inspect the zip before excluding it for good.

name: ICSI Meeting Corpus
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Downloadable from the Edinburgh ICSI page: annotations as NXT zips, audio per meeting (headset mix about 120 MB or individual headset SPH about 350 MB per meeting)
notes: Hosted by the University of Edinburgh AMI group; the LDC release is ICSI Meeting Speech (LDC2004S02, transcripts LDC2004T04). Annotations: ICSI core NXT v1.0 (2016-07-22, transcripts and dialogue acts), core plus contributed annotations (topic, hotspot, summaries), original MRT transcripts. The overview, signals, data-present and annotation-present pages linked from the ICSI site describe the AMI corpus, not ICSI. The LDC catalogue gives about 72 h of speech in 75 meetings (883 h of audio over all channels) and, besides the close-talking microphones, six table-top microphones; the Edinburgh page describes the close-talking audio only (recording_setup close_talk follows it). Most meetings include read digit strings in the same wave files: exclude them or score them separately

name: USC IEMOCAP
status_note: Lab copy (Session1-5, documentation) on the lab's shared corpus storage. Who signed the release form for it is not known
notes: Acted dyadic dialogues (improvised and scripted), five sessions, ten actors; about 12 hours per the survey (not checked). Mostly used for emotion recognition; same lab (Busso) as MSP-Conversation.

name: IFA Dialog Video corpus (IFADV)
status_note: Free download from the UvA IFA corpora website.
notes: Also awd (automatic word/phoneme alignment, TextGrid), EAF gaze annotations, functional dialog-act annotation, video (two gen-locked cameras). Original sound 48 kHz 16-bit PCM. Sessions start with "some scripted sentences" before free talk. Copyright transferred to the Dutch Language Union (Nederlandse Taalunie). LREC 2008 paper: van Son et al., "The IFADV corpus: A free dialog video corpus".

name: IMDA National Speech Corpus (NSC), conversational part (Part 3)
status_note: Register with IMDA (nsc@imda.gov.sg); the corpus is shared as a Dropbox folder by email (Dropbox account required).
notes: Paper: "around 1000 hours of conversational speech" (approximate; not in hours_reported); sessions "approximately 2 hours 15 minutes long"; mics 48 kHz down-sampled to 16 kHz, telephones 8 kHz. IMDA FAQ: NSC "approximately 1.2 TB", 6 parts since the July 2021 update (the extra parts were not described on the pages opened). Paper (2019) describes the conversational part as not yet released and transcription in progress; per-speaker transcript timing and file format were not seen. Code-switching present.

name: Indic DiarBench
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Public Hugging Face dataset (test splits only)
notes: Joint diarization and ASR benchmark for the 22 scheduled languages of India, about 108 hours (card: approximately 108 hours; 1.1-12.6 h per language) in near-field, far-field and in-the-wild conditions (in-the-wild about 28 h, 10 languages). Clips cut from the same source recording share a recording_id.

name: Kallaama (Wolof, Pulaar, Sereer)
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. OpenSLR 151
notes: Agricultural radio programmes, focus groups and interviews (Wolof 55 h, Pulaar about 32 h, Sereer; about 125 h in all per the survey). Whether the transcripts mark speaker turns with times was not checked: turn_source left empty, so it is not yet usable as diarization data.

name: Kenya/Philippines English Dialogue (Reord-AI)
status_note: Hugging Face, gated (automatic approval after accepting conditions). Card readable on the dataset web page; raw README needs login.
notes: Card: "Total duration: ~65 hours", "Speakers: >150; ~15 PH, remaining KE". Total file size 23.8 GB. Caveat: "A Kenyan interviewee who's connection drops will appear across multiple tracks in the same room" and "Speakers will be clustered in the next release" — track IDs are not speaker IDs. Audio Opus 48 kHz transcoded to pcm_s16le, segments only (1-30 s) so silences between segments are dropped; rebuilding a session timeline needs START/END from the key. No transcripts mentioned. Contact hello@datai.world.

name: Who Speaks When? (LIAS, French)
status_note: GitHub (annotations only); audio rebuilt per subset: ParisStories by script, VoxPopuli from the official VoxPopuli download, Kaamelott from the user's own copy of the episodes.
notes: Subsets: ParisStories 2022 (20 files; spontaneous anecdotes, source corpus has "monologues and dialogues"; diarization converted from the source .conllu; audio downloaded by script from links in metadata.json). Kaamelott (16 TV-series excerpts; "générées automatiquement ... puis corrigées et vérifiées manuellement"; audio and transcripts not redistributable, user must obtain episodes). VoxPopuli (220 sessions; "Conversations multi-locuteurs synthétiques" built by concatenating same-day parliament monologues; automatic labels) — simulated, not real conversation. Hours not stated. Benchmark-oriented (ASR + diarization evaluation).

name: LibriCSS
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Downloadable from Google Drive through dataprep.sh in the repository
notes: LibriSpeech test-clean utterances concatenated into conversations and replayed from loudspeakers in a meeting room, recorded with a 7-channel circular array (Microsoft, ICASSP 2020). Each 1-hour session has six 10-minute mini sessions with overlap ratios 0S, 0L, 10, 20, 30 and 40% (overlap over total speech); 52 to 125 utterances per mini session; ground-truth utterance boundaries are provided. Built for evaluating continuous speech separation; must not be used for training. Our librispeech_meetings_sim uses LibriSpeech training speakers only, so it does not overlap

name: LibriSpeech
status_note: Single-speaker read speech; kept as source material for simulated mixtures
notes: Read English audiobook speech (LibriVox), about 1000 hours, subsets dev/test/train clean and other with disjoint speakers (README.TXT 2). One reader per file, so not usable as diarization data; used as speech source for librispeech_meetings_sim (training subsets only) and the source of LibriCSS (test-clean) and Sparse LibriMix (test-clean)

name: synth-librispeech-meetings
status_note: Lab-internal simulation on scratch storage, which is purged: copy the clean and reverb conditions to permanent storage before relying on them. Lhotse manifests (recordings, supervisions, cuts) per condition, and RTTM per shard in the out/ directories. Lives outside SD_DATA_ROOT
notes: Four conditions of 3000 meetings each: clean, noise, reverb, noise_reverb (the same meetings under each). Speech-hours union 25.87% overlapped; 2580527 supervisions with word alignments. Sources counted from the clean supervisions: 2334 speakers, from train-clean-100, train-clean-360 and train-other-500 (no dev or test speakers). Manifests store absolute audio paths

name: MagicData-RAMC
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage: the lab directory named magicdata holds a different corpus, MAGICDATA Mandarin Chinese Read Speech (read speech with TRANS.txt and SPKINFO.txt), not RAMC
notes: Each speaker takes part in up to three conversations (paper Sec. 2.2). Split hours in the paper's table: 149.65 / 9.89 / 20.64. OpenSLR 123 (re-read 2026-10-31, all values agree): recorded on mobile phones in a quiet indoor environment, transcriptions proofed by professional inspectors, train/validation/test in a ratio of 15:1:2, speaker and topic metadata included

name: MISP-M3SD
status_note: Hugging Face Igor97/MISP-M3SD, gated (auto-approve after sharing contact info): audio.zip + 6 split parts (73.8 GB total), oracle.rttm, split.txt; videos only as IDs/scripts.
notes: Splits: Train 1272 samples 716.54 h; Dev 50 / 27.10 h; Eval 50 / 26.91 h. Uploader: HF user Igor97, profile full name "Hang Chen" (HF users API); companion GitHub coalboss/MISP-M3SD, whose owner is "Hang Chen, University of Science and Technology of China, USTC"; the pipeline uses the MISP 2022 AVSD baseline. Hang Chen is a known MISP challenge organiser, but no MISP page opened here names this dataset, so the link to the MISP organisers is by name only. Predecessor M3SD (Shilong Wu, arXiv 2506.14427; GitHub slwu0209/M3SD) describes the same 770+ h: "The data comes from YouTube and is pseudo-labeled through a variety of speaker diarization systems" (3D-Speaker + MISP AVSD + DOVER-Lap) and "the speaker diarization labels of the data are not manually annotated". MISP-M3SD adds "selective manual verification"; how much was verified is not stated. Card readable without login; files gated.

name: Mixer 6 Speech
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Re-judged on 2026-11-04 under the conversation scope: the conversational telephone calls have one channel per call side, so turns can come from VAD; the interviews (14 room microphones) and transcript readings cannot. The diarization-ready interview subset is mixer6_chime8 (LDC2025S07)
notes: Collected by LDC in 2009-2010 (Mixer phase 6, native American English speakers near Philadelphia). 4,410 telephone calls (8 kHz 2-channel SPHERE, robot-operator protocol like Switchboard-2) and 1,425 multi-microphone office sessions (14 synchronised microphones, 16 kHz FLAC) with repeat questions, a 15-minute informal conversation, a 15-minute transcript reading and a call. Used in the NIST SRE 2010 test sets. Its recordings are reused by DIHARD II and III and by LDC2025S07

name: Mixer 6 - CHiME 8 Transcribed Calls and Interviews
status_note: Lab copy of the CHiME-7/8 version of Mixer 6 (README: full annotation for the dev and eval sets as used in the CHiME-7 and 8 DASR challenges): archives and split lists; the extracted transcription folders are empty. Whether it matches the LDC release LDC2025S07 is not checked. The diarization-ready subset of Mixer 6 Speech (LDC2013S03)
notes: Built for CHiME-7 Task 1 and CHiME-8 Task 1 (released 2025-08-15). Development and test sets are fully transcribed multi-microphone interviews, speaker-disjoint from training. Recorded on 13 of Mixer 6's microphones. Overlap to check: DIHARD III also reuses Mixer 6 recordings (its evaluation set is evaluation-only, its development set is training data)

name: MSDWild
status_note: Evaluation only (maintainer decision 2026-11-01). Needs the MSDWild licence agreement signed and sent to X-LANCE (SJTU) before download: maintainer decision. The agreement grants research-only use without redistribution and states that the video's original creator is the sole owner of the copyright. Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Audio 7.56 GB, raw videos 43.14 GB, cropped faces 14.49 GB on Google Drive
notes: YouTube VLog clips, one continuous scene each (PySceneDetect), at least two speakers, filtered by hand. 91.29% speech; 11.8 speaker changes per minute. Only speech is labelled (no laughter or singing); off-screen speech and single words are labelled. The many-talker set is for testing only. Supplementary frame-by-frame face boxes (2024-01-08) and cropped faces for active speaker detection. RTTM files in the repository list 3,143 sessions (2,476 / 490 / 177 by split)

name: MSP-Conversation
status_note: Lab copy: Release v1.1 (244 conversations, 59 h 33 min; 695 diarization JSON files). The current release is 2.0 (310 conversations, 77 h 26 min; MSP-Conversation page). Before using the lab copy, find out who signed the agreement for it: the agreement covers only the Recipient Scientist and people under their direct supervision. No RTTM: convert the JSON turns
notes: Conversations are 10-20 min excerpts of MSP-Podcast podcasts, split into 3-7 min parts for annotation; speaker turns are given per part. Also has continuous arousal/valence/dominance ratings. Languages and license are not stated in the readme; not checked elsewhere. The lab copy also has a transcripts_whisper folder that the readme does not list

name: Multi-TPC (three-party conversations)
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Open Zenodo record
notes: Three-party conversations with speech, motion capture and gaze; one 44.1 kHz WAV and one word-timed transcript per participant; frame-level speaking activity per participant in AudioGazeGBack. About 5.3 h per the survey (not checked here).

name: Multimodal Earnings Call Dataset (2018–2024)
status_note: Zenodo, open download, four yearly zips (2018-2021) currently posted.
notes: README says "Companies: ~200", "Earnings calls: ~8100", "Total compressed size: ~114 GB", archives 2018-2024, but record 19032377 (and the other version 19030119) hold only dataset_2018-2021.zip (≈43.9 GB) and metadata.csv with 4,031 call rows. transcript.csv end_time is the START time of the last word of the speaker turn (code takes start_times[-1]), so turn ends are slightly early. Data was fetched with the `earningscall` Python API (get_transcript level 3/4 + audio). Speaker count per call not stated. Code repo licence AGPL-3.0 (GitHub API).

name: NB Samtale (Norwegian Conversation Speech Corpus)
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Public Hugging Face dataset
notes: Released as segments (wav per segment), not as full recordings; each segment names its source file and its start and end time in it, so a session timeline can be rebuilt with silence between segments. Speaker IDs are global across files.

name: NOTSOFAR-1
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Download from the Hugging Face dataset microsoft/NOTSOFAR with an access token (utils/notsofar_dataset.py)
notes: Microsoft, CHiME-8 Task 2 (Interspeech 2024). Meetings average 6 minutes in 30 rooms; each meeting is recorded by several devices, a device recording of one meeting being a session (paper: about 150 h single-channel and 110 h multi-channel over all sessions). Evaluation speakers and rooms are disjoint from training and development; 10 of dev1's 12 speakers are in training. Metadata hashtags (e.g. #DebateOverlaps, #TalkNearWhiteboard). Also released: a simulated training set of about 1,000 hours with 15,000 real acoustic transfer functions, using MOS-filtered LibriVox speech (500 h), not recorded here as a row. Mc_rockfall_1 is excluded from the evaluation sets

name: Norwegian Parliamentary Speech Corpus (NPSC)
status_note: Lab copy: 41 meeting days with full audio, sentence and token JSON and the NPSC documentation, on the lab's shared corpus storage
notes: Whole days of Stortinget meetings (140.3 h with pauses, 125.7 h without). Turn-taking is mostly sequential (speeches and replies), so overlap is likely low. Speaker IDs link to the official release's speaker metadata.

name: AMERICAN ENGLISH TRANSCRIBED HI-FI FULL-DUPLEX TWO-SPEAKER CONVERSATIONAL DATASET — SAMPLE (Ocular AI)
status_note: Hugging Face, gated with manual approval; card readable on the web page, raw README needs login.
notes: Tracks start at different times: apply per-track offsets from filename capture timestamps (later speaker offsets 1.321, 2.125, 2.109, 1.298 s) — "Do not align both files to zero if studying overlap". FLAC mono per speaker; 120.64 min of track audio. Sample of a larger commercial Ocular collection (see also the CC-BY-NC ~230 h OcularAIInc/AmericanEnglishFullDuplexTwoSpeakerConversationalDataset). "Separate microphone capture is not a guarantee of zero acoustic bleed."

name: Open Yap 1K
status_note: Lab copy (75 GB archive) on the lab's shared corpus storage. Who signed the data use agreement for it is not known
notes: Dual-channel English conversations at 48 kHz. Word timings are automatic (Deepgram Nova-3); some conversations also have human transcripts with per-turn segments but no word timings. The lab copy is one 75 GB FLAC archive (open-yap-1k, dated 2026-09-11) and a conversations directory that this account cannot read.

name: Rasheed Mudasiru multi-speaker recording (SLR162)
status_note: OpenSLR SLR162, free download (400 MB zip).
notes: Undergraduate project (Federal University of Technology Minna). The 63 min is cut into 190 WAV clips (sizes 44 B to 4.8 MB; one is header-only). Could serve only as unlabeled multi-speaker audio.

name: otoSpeech-full-duplex-280h
status_note: Gated on Hugging Face (automatic approval after a form). Not on the lab's shared corpus storage
notes: Full-duplex English conversations in WebDataset shards (data/train). Per the survey (card not readable without access): about 280 hours of raw audio with one channel per speaker and some muted redacted segments; a processed 141 h version (otoSpeech-full-duplex-processed-141h, also CC BY 4.0) may overlap it. Neither checked here: turn_source left empty until the card is read after accepting the gate.

name: otoSpeech-full-duplex-task-oriented-20h
status_note: Hugging Face otoearth, gated with an auto-approved form (name, organisation, intended use, commercial use).
notes: Extends otoSpeech-full-duplex-280h (already in the DB as otospeech_fd_280h) with task state and interaction events aligned to the recording timeline. v2 "contains sessions collected after the latest session" in the 20h release; "The 58 sessions from that release are not duplicated in v2." The session JSON holds task events with timestamps; whether it holds per-speaker speech segments was not seen (card gated for files). Microphone type not stated (channel-separated remote sessions).

name: otoSpeech-full-duplex-task-oriented-v2
status_note: Hugging Face otoearth, gated with an auto-approved form (name, organisation, intended use, commercial use).
notes: Extends otoSpeech-full-duplex-280h (already in the DB as otospeech_fd_280h) with task state and interaction events aligned to the recording timeline. v2 "contains sessions collected after the latest session" in the 20h release; "The 58 sessions from that release are not duplicated in v2." The session JSON holds task events with timestamps; whether it holds per-speaker speech segments was not seen (card gated for files). Microphone type not stated (channel-separated remote sessions).

name: Perit Duplex Support Conversations (English)
status_note: HF sample open (3.5 GB); full set via form on perit.ai/datasets.
notes: Channel-to-role mapping varies (38 of 45 open on left). Stereo 48 kHz WAV, loudness-normalised jointly; studio-clean. Full set "15.5 hours / 180 conversations in the same format is free on request at https://perit.ai/datasets — one form" (licence of the full set not read). Only 8 voices.

name: PriMock57
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Public GitHub repository
notes: Mock consultations between clinicians and actors playing patients (role-played, not scripted). Separate doctor and patient tracks were reported by the survey but not checked here.

name: Real-TurnTurk
status_note: Hugging Face, open.
notes: Per-speaker Opus webm 48 kHz; cross-channel bleed 73-78 dB below own level. speech_activity.csv is Silero VAD (automatic) on a 62.5 ms grid; how text.csv timings were produced is not stated (annotation_method left unset). Overlap 7.0% simultaneous speech. Speakers recur across recordings (p01, p06 in three each). Facial-feature CSVs and animations included; 3.0 GB total.

name: 2003 NIST Rich Transcription Evaluation Data
status_note: Lab copy of LDC2007S10: audio, input UEMs (including expt_03_spkr_* for diarization) and references (MDTM, CTM, STM, a few RTTM). Not measured: the speaker references are MDTM
notes: Evaluation data only: the test material of the 2003 NIST Rich Transcription Spring (RT-03S) and Fall (RT-03F) evaluations (LDC catalogue, re-read 2026-10-31; released 2007-08-17). Speaker diarization was evaluated on English only: broadcast news about 3 h (30-minute excerpts from six TDT-4 broadcasts of February 2001) and CTS about 6 h (5-minute excerpts from 72 conversations: 36 Switchboard Cellular, 36 Fisher). The Mandarin and Arabic sets (about 1 h each of BN and CTS; CTS from CallFriend Mandarin and CallHome Egyptian Arabic) were for STT. CTS audio holds only the excerpts, 2-channel 8-bit mu-law SPHERE. The CTS diarization task is no longer supported by NIST (deemed degenerate); the diarization references were updated after RT-03S

name: Mandarin-English Code-Switching in South-East Asia (SEAME)
status_note: Lab copy of LDC2015S04 on the lab's shared corpus storage
notes: Conversational and interview speech (lab copy: data/conversation and data/interview). Whether each speaker has a channel of their own and whether the transcripts carry speaker-attributed times was not checked: turn_source left empty.

name: Seamless Interaction
status_note: Lab copy of the improvised and naturalistic sessions, train, dev and test: one wav, mp4, npz and JSON per participant (improvised 35750, naturalistic 93620 participants). No RTTM: derive turns from the per-participant VAD or word times in the JSON
notes: Meta, 2025. Over 4,000 hours from more than 4,000 participants in two labels, improvised (scenario prompts with at least one professional actor) and naturalistic (prompted conversations). Per participant: 1080p video, denoised 48 kHz audio on a separate channel, time-aligned transcript (JSONL), VAD (100 Hz), SMPL-H, keypoints and movement features; some files have first- and third-party internal-state annotations. Whole dataset about 27 TB; dev and test 5 batches each, train 200+. The language is not stated in the README. The lab copy (improvised only, audio and JSON) has 2-channel wav files per interaction

name: Simsamu
status_note: Open on Hugging Face medkit/simsamu.
notes: Role-play by emergency medicine interns (not real calls); seven caller communication modes (shy, angry, frightened, ...). Audio 8 kHz m4a, average 3 min 11 s per recording. RTTM labels are role names (medecin, patient_1, ...); metadata.csv gives speaker ids. Annotation method (manual vs automatic) not stated. speech_style: unscripted role-play, recorded as spontaneous. LICENSE: "MIT License Copyright (c) 2023 HeKA Research Team".

name: snorbyte audio dialog / natural-conversation samples
status_note: Hugging Face, gated (automatic approval). Cards readable on the web pages.
notes: Three gated repos (all CC BY 4.0, auto gate): indic-audio-dialog-sample ("over 30 hours", 2,193 files ~9.8 GB, read GPT-4.1 translations), indic-audio-natural-conversations-sample ("over 6 hours", ~2.0 GB; speakers "not strictly constrained to the exact wording"), world-audio-natural-conversations-sample (it, es; ~0.62 GB). All described as "multichannel, source-separated"; the per-line ZIP clips suggest lines were recorded one at a time and stitched (not confirmed without downloading). Could serve as clean per-speaker speech for simulation.

name: SpiCE: Speech in Cantonese and English
status_note: Free download from Borealis (Scholars Portal) Dataverse, doi 10.5683/SP2/MJOXP3.
notes: 34 early Cantonese-English bilinguals (participants), one interviewer (Nancy Yiu) for all sessions, so the interviewer channel is the same speaker throughout. Each file also contains read sentences and a storyboard narration before the interview (task tier marks them). One file is mono (participant only). Hours not stated (34 x 2 x ~25-30 min interview, my estimate ~30 h). Identifying content silenced and marked xxx.

name: Spjallrómur - Icelandic Conversational Speech
status_note: Free download from CLARIN-IS (version 26.03, 2.27 GB); GitHub icelandic-lt/spjallromur holds the revised re-aligned version and the ASR/diarization recipes.
notes: Full conversations: "18 hrs 20 mins of 46 full conversations, 92 speakers"; half conversations "2 hrs 42 mins with 7 conversations"; unaligned "1 hr and 16 mins with 3 recordings" (GitHub README). Speakers used their own microphones/devices over an online platform; "some picked up background noise from neighboring speakers"; small length mismatches between the two files "due to some network lag". CLARIN 26.03 (hdl 20.500.12537/379, issued 2026-03-02): "additional manual transcriptions for 21 full conversations, produced by three transcribers. Includes turn-level timestamps and speaker labels. Seven conversations have multiple transcriptions". Original 22.01 is hdl 20.500.12537/187 (replaced by 379). PII bleeped with a 400 Hz tone.

name: SpokenWOZ
status_note: Lab copy (train_dev and test audio and text) on the lab's shared corpus storage
notes: Task-oriented human-to-human dialogues (MultiWOZ-style). Turn and word times come from the ASR transcription.

name: Switchboard-1 Release 2
status_note: Lab copy of LDC97S62 (Release 2, README dated August 1997): 2438 SPHERE files, transcriptions and word alignments. Speaker segments must be derived from the per-channel transcripts
notes: Texas Instruments, 1990-1991; Release 2 (LDC, 1993) corrects Release 1 and its speaker attribution table; three missing files (sw02289, sw04361, sw04379) were added on 2013-03-26 and converted to unshortened SPHERE on 2015-08-11 (catalogue). 543 speakers (302 male, 241 female) from all US regions; about 70 topics. The ISIP MS98 transcripts and word alignments are the usual source for turn times; the lab copy has them. Used in Hub5 LVCSR and NIST SRE projects. Maintainer decision 2026-10-30: training, internal only; no official split

name: Tamil-English Code-Mixed Podcast Diarization Dataset
status_note: Hugging Face, open; 2 WAV + 2 RTTM.
notes: "~2.5 hours total" over 2 recordings. Sources: youtube.com/watch?v=buG3n_srRtI and lI2L6DLvQGU. Also labels/*.txt per file. Card says the YouTube videos were "released under Creative Commons Attribution licenses" (not verified on YouTube). Out-of-scope: "Commercial redistribution".

name: ViYT-Diar (Vietnamese YouTube Diarization Dataset)
status_note: Hugging Face, open (one test parquet split).
notes: Hours not stated (test parquet 307.7 MB, 16 kHz mono WAV). Described as "exclusively designed to serve as a high-quality test benchmark". Paper: Thang et al., MAPR 2025, "Adapting WavLM for Vietnamese Speaker Diarization in Real-world Conversations" (no URL opened).

name: VoxConverse
status_note: Lab copy of the dev and test audio; no RTTM in the copy (they are in the GitHub repository)
notes: Paper: 91% of video time is speech and 3-4% of speech is overlapped; 4-6 speakers per video on average, up to 21. v0.3 fixes errors in some test RTTM files (README)

name: VoxMM
status_note: Request a key via the KAIST form linked from the project page; preprocessing code at github.com/kaistmm/VoxMM.
notes: Stats v1.0.0: Dev "6,094" min of utterances, 247 videos, 2,253 speakers; Test "462" min, 42 videos, 374 speakers (about 109 h of utterance time). Language is not stated on the page (likely mostly English; unconfirmed). "video files are not included in this dataset"; that audio is included is implied but not stated outright. v1.1.0 (2026-10-07) updated face tracks only. Content includes "political debates and news". Authors include S. Watanabe.
